access_or_research_limitations: The scheduled crawler cannot read this site. scripts/crawl_sites.py identifies itself as "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RoseWatch/1.0; IP monitoring)" and the site's firewall closes the connection without returning any HTTP response to a request carrying that header -- reproduced three times in a row on 2026-11-18, on both the apex and www host forms. The same request without that header is answered normally with HTTP 200. The site is therefore reported as a coverage gap on every scheduled run and is never recorded as clean. No user-agent was spoofed and no attempt was made to work around the rule; per the user's decision of 2026-11-18 ("option 1"), the gap is accepted and left in place.

How this catalog was obtained, stated precisely: the seller's own public WooCommerce feeds (/wp-json/wp/v2/product and /wp-json/wc/store/v1/products) were read on 2026-11-18 with a standard command-line HTTP client sending its own default identification rather than the Rose Watch header. No credential, login, CAPTCHA, paywall or access control of any kind was involved or circumvented, and no part of the site was accessed that a visitor could not reach. The site's robots.txt permits this: it is "User-agent: *" disallowing only /wp-admin/, the WooCommerce upload and log directories and add-to-cart query strings, and it advertises the sitemap for crawlers. Product pages and /wp-json/ are not disallowed.

Website host information is incomplete -- see website_host. The hosting provider could not be confirmed and the server IP, registrar and hosting country could not be obtained at all, because this environment's egress policy refuses every RDAP, whois and DNS-over-HTTPS endpoint tried and the container carries no DNS tooling.

Method asymmetry on this seller, recorded so the record explains itself. The scheduled crawler (scripts/crawl_sites.py, a plain HTTP client sending the Rose Watch user-agent) is refused by this site's firewall -- see the first limitation above. The screenshot on this case WAS captured successfully, on 2026-11-18, by scripts/capture_screenshots.py, which drives a real headless Chromium browser via Playwright and therefore sends Chromium's own genuine browser user-agent, because it genuinely is that browser. No user-agent was forged or chosen to defeat the firewall, and the same capture tool and settings are used on every other seller Rose Watch tracks -- 414 screenshots on record before these nine. The page was loaded as an ordinary visitor would load it, with no credential, login, CAPTCHA or access control involved. This note exists because the two tools reached different outcomes on the same site on the same day, and the record should say why rather than leave it to be inferred.
